texts: doha about people shouting their prayers on loudspeakers like God is deaf
Why climb up and shout the call to prayer at the top of your voice, as though the Lord were deaf and could not hear the whisper of a sincere heart in the dark?
shouting at a deaf God
Every dawn the loudspeaker at the end of our lane wakes the whole colony, and my newborn cries. I keep thinking God surely hears quieter things. Doha?
Is the Beloved so hard of hearing that He needs a thundering voice to find you?

Write about those who chant at the top of their voices beside the cremation ground, waking the dead with their noise, as if the Lord were deaf, while a cloth sheet covers the silent one who now hears only silence.
At the cremation ground near us, a group chanted so loudly that people walking past covered their ears, and a cloth sheet over the body lay perfectly still. Doha on that?
doha: cremation ground, cloth sheet, shouting prayers
cremation ground, cloth sheet, shouting
The cloth sheet lies silent on the cremation ground, but the living shout as if the Lord were farther than the grave.
The sun rises in silence and the pearl forms in silence, yet man shouts to the heavens as though the Lord were deaf.
sun, pearl, shouting prayer
A doha about the quiet sun rising and the quiet pearl growing in the oyster, both done without a sound, while we scream our prayers and call it devotion, as though the Lord could not hear silence.
doha: the sun rises quietly and pearls grow quietly but people pray with loudspeakers
I woke at sunrise to the sound of loudspeakers while wearing my mother's pearl earrings for a wedding, and thought how gentle the morning could have been. A doha?

Compose a verse about the chakor bird, which gazes at the sky in silent longing, and the cloud passing without a sound, while men below shout their chants as though God were deaf to the quiet of devotion.
chakor bird, cloud, shouting
A chakor bird sat silent on our roof while a cloud drifted and the neighbours' loud jagran carried on until three in the morning. I felt the bird knew more about God. A doha?
doha: the chakor bird and a cloud are silent but people shout their prayers
The chakor bird gazes without a word, the cloud passes without a sound, and man shouts at a Lord who is not deaf.
Why do you shout your prayers from the roof of your house, as though the Lord were deaf, when He dwells in the quiet room of your own heart and hears every breath you take?
house, loud prayer
The man in the house next to ours holds his devotional singing with a microphone at midnight every Thursday, and we can't sleep. A doha for him?
The house trembles with the noise of praise while the Beloved waits in the silence of the heart.
doha: shouting prayers inside the house through a mic, is God deaf?
deaf God, loud chants
A doha for those who think the Lord can only hear them if they chant until their throats are raw, shouting the holy names in the streets as though a whisper had never reached the divine ear.
My uncle's chanting group practises at full volume every evening, and the dogs howl along. He says God must be woken up. What would Kabir say?
He shouts the Name until his voice cracks, as if the Lord had wandered far from his ear.
doha pls about shouting your chants at God
doha: loud prayer at the bier and the spinning wheel quietly turning, who is closer to God
bier, spinning wheel, shouting
At my uncle's last rites the reciters chanted so loudly beside the bier that my aunt could not hear her own grief, while in the corner her spinning wheel stood silent. A doha?

A doha on the loud chanting around the bier and the spinning wheel that turns without a sound, honest work done in quiet being nearer to the Lord than the thunder of those who shout as if He were deaf.
Beside the bier they shout, beside the spinning wheel there is silence; which is nearer the Lord?
Please write a doha on the man who raises his voice in prayer in the early dawn, loud enough to wake the whole neighbourhood, who believes that the Lord is far away and must be reached by shouting.
loud dawn prayer
doha: god is not deaf, stop shouting prayers
My grandmother, who prays in a whisper, says her prayers have never needed anyone's microphone. She was reacting to a loud religious event in the park. A doha?
A whisper in the heart travels farther than a shout across the town.
Louder and louder rises the prayer, but God, who sits within, is not deaf; only the shouting heart is.
A doha on how the man who shouts the loudest in his devotions is often the most deaf to the cries of the poor and sick around him, though he believes the Lord must be addressed in thunder.
shouting man, deaf heart
write a doha: the loudest prayer is the emptiest
Our local religious leader has the loudest voice at every festival and yet ignored the old woman who was crying outside his gate. What would Kabir say?
loud chants, quiet God
The drum beats, the voices rise, and the Lord sits unmoved in the silence behind them.
doha: God is quiet, people are loud, funny contrast
Last night's festival procession blasted music until two in the morning, and the sick old man next lane could not sleep. Doha for him?
A doha on the festival crowds whose drums and chants shake the street for hours, who believe that the louder the sound, the nearer the Lord, though the Lord has always been found in stillness.
A group of young men in our colony shout slogans of faith through a megaphone every evening, and I think their God must be quite far if they need that. Could you write a doha?
Write a doha on the folly of thinking that a loud voice makes a strong faith, as the Lord who hears the footsteps of an ant has no need of the thunder of men.
Is the Lord an old man who cannot hear, that you must storm the sky with your voice?
doha on megaphone prayers and how silly it is
megaphone faith
The wedding at the palace hall next to our colony played religious chants on loudspeakers until the early hours, and the bride's father was sleeping on the stairs, tired. A doha?
doha: palace wedding with loud chanting all night, pointless
Write a doha about the rich man's palace where chanting is played at full volume to announce his piety to the neighbours, though the Lord hears only the whisper of a poor man's honest prayer.
In the great palace the chanting shakes the walls, and the Lord, quite unmoved, waits in the quiet.
palace, loud chanting
My friend turned up the volume of his devotional songs until the whole block could hear, and said it was an offering. I said, 'To whom?' A doha for that exchange?
Turn down the voice and turn up the heart, and the Beloved will hear you from the next room.
Please write a doha on those who believe that raising the volume of their devotion makes it holier, forgetting that the Lord listens not to the loudness of the voice but to the honesty behind it.
volume is not devotion
doha: turning up the volume on prayer doesn't make it holier
The ocean roars and the bitter gourd grows silent; man shouts his prayers but remains bitter within.
The bitter gourd soup my mother made was served with loud chanting from the neighbours and a wedding, near the ocean, and I thought, what is all this noise for? A doha?
doha: ocean roars but prayers should be quiet, bitter gourd people shout
ocean, bitter gourd, shouting
A doha on how the ocean roars in its depths and yet is calm in its soul, while the man who shouts his chants beside it remains as bitter as a bitter gourd, deaf to the silence of the Lord.
Write a doha about the bee that hums softly as it goes about its work among the flowers and finds sweetness, and the man who shouts his prayers for hours and finds no sweetness at all in the Name.
doha: bee hums quietly and still finds honey, loud prayers dont work
A bee kept humming over the flowers in my garden while the neighbours' loud religious music played, and I felt the bee was more devoted than the whole crowd. A doha?
The bee hums low and finds the honey; the man cries loud and finds the noise.
bee, shouted prayers
A doha about the one who shouts his prayers from a mountain top, hoping the Lord will hear better, though the Lord is as near in a quiet valley, or in the pain of a thorn, as on any peak.
mountain, thorn, shouting
On a trek up a mountain, a group shouted their chants from the summit, and I had a thorn in my foot and I prayed quietly. Mine felt closer. A doha?
doha: you can shout from a mountain or feel a thorn, God is quiet
Shout from the mountain top or sit with a thorn in the foot, the Lord's ear is the same.
A verse about the bee that does not shout when it finds a flower and the man who shouts to find his Lord, as though the Lord were far away and deaf and the bee closer to Him than man.
bee, shouting prayer
My friend said he would out shout anyone with his prayer, and just then a bee landed on his arm and he went quiet. Doha for that moment?
doha: bee is quiet, man is loud with his prayers
The bee is quiet in its devotion, and the man is loud in his; one of them gets honey.
doha: a thread of silent prayer is stronger than a loud chant
My aunt stitches in silence, thread by thread, and calls it her prayer, while the neighbours shout their chants all day. Doha for her?
A doha on the fine thread of a quiet prayer, spun without a sound in the heart, which reaches the Lord more surely than the loud chorus of voices that men raise in their hundreds.
thread, silent prayer
One quiet thread of prayer from the heart is worth a thousand voices thrown at the sky.
shouting, as if deaf
Why does the man in the street shout his hymns at the sky as if God were hard of hearing, and the Beloved who knows his every thought were sitting at the far end of a crowded hall?
My cousin's religious group parades through the streets at night with drums and microphones, and I thought, does their God have bad hearing? A doha?
doha pls: the God is not deaf, why shout
Do you call a friend who sits beside you from across the town?
He calls to the Lord from rooftops, though the Lord sits in the ear of his own heart.
roof-top shouting
doha about shouting hymns from the rooftop
A doha about the man who stands on his roof at dawn and shouts his devotion over the town, as though the Lord were somewhere far over the horizon and could not hear the quiet one beside him.
The man across from us stands on his terrace each morning with a loud speaker for his devotional songs, and it wakes the entire street. A doha for him?
At the funeral, the loud chanting did not let us hear the potter's quiet words about his late father, who made clay wares for fifty years and wore a shroud like a simple man. A doha?
A doha about the potter who shapes clay in silence and the shroud that wraps the dead without a sound, set against the noisy shouting of men who believe that the Lord is deaf to a quiet heart.
doha: potter and clay are silent, shroud is silent, but men shout prayers
potter and clay, shroud, noise
The potter shapes the clay in silence, the shroud is folded in silence, but man storms heaven with his voice.
In the evening my neighbour recites his prayers at the top of his voice so that everyone will know how holy he is. Honestly, it seems more like a performance. A doha?
He prays aloud so the street may hear, but the Lord needs no audience.
Write a doha on the person who raises his voice in prayer so that all around him can hear and admire, who is praying not to the Lord but to the crowd that listens.
prayer for the crowd
doha: praying loud so others can hear
forehead mark, temple, loud
A doha on the one with a bright forehead mark who shouts his chants at the temple gate for all to hear, though the Lord within the temple is neither deaf nor impressed by the volume.
doha: loud chants at the temple and a big forehead mark, show off
The man with the biggest forehead mark at our temple has the loudest voice during aarti, and the elderly worshippers move away because of it. A doha?
The forehead mark is bright and the voice is loud, but the Lord sits in the quiet corner of the temple.
The weaver in our lane works silently at his loom all day, but the man across the way shouts the holy names with his hoarse tongue so loudly that the weaver can barely think. A doha?
The loom is silent as it weaves, but the tongue that shouts has woven nothing.
A doha on the loom that makes cloth without a word and the tongue that shouts holy names without a thought, with the Lord's blessing falling on the weaver's quiet work and not on the noise.
doha: weaver's loom is quiet, tongue is loud, who is closer to God
loom, tongue, loud prayer
doha: lion roars but doesn't shout prayers, humans do
The lion roars because it is a lion; man roars at the Lord because he is afraid.
A doha about the lion whose roar comes from its true nature, and the man whose shouted prayers come from his fear, trying to wake a Lord who was never asleep and could never be deaf.
lion, shouting prayer
The lion at the zoo roared and the whole crowd went quiet, while the people shouting prayers at the nearby festival went on. I thought, that lion is more honest. Could you write a doha?
loud devotion, empty heart
Louder and louder the praise, emptier and emptier the heart.
doha on loud prayer and empty hearts
The family that organises the neighbourhood religious event is the one that never visits the sick, and they have the biggest speakers. A doha?
A doha about the volume of devotion in the street that grows louder every year while sincerity in the heart grows quieter, and the Lord who hears the heart is not moved by the noise.
prayer beads, loud prayer
doha: prayer beads in one hand and a loudspeaker in the other lol
A doha about the person who rolls prayer beads and chants at full volume, so that all the neighbours know how many rounds he has done, though the Lord knows only the silence in his mind.
Mr. Verma sits on his balcony every morning with prayer beads, chanting so loudly that the whole building knows when he has finished. Doha for him?
The prayer beads turn, the voice thunders, and the heart sits silent behind both.
A crow cawed loudly on our window sill during the loud chanting from the next street, and my daughter said, 'Is the crow also praying?' A doha for her?
A doha on the crow which caws as loudly as it can at the dawn without pretending to be holy, and the man who shouts his prayers with equal volume and calls it devotion.
The crow caws at the dawn and the pious shout at the dawn; the crow at least is honest.
doha: crow caws loud and people shout prayers loud, same noise
crow, loud prayer
doha: quiet prayer is better than shouting
Be still, for the Lord is not far.
silence is prayer
When my grandfather was ill, we all sat in silence at his bedside and prayed quietly, and it felt more powerful than any of the loud festivals we had attended. A doha?
A doha that teaches how a silent prayer from the depth of the heart is heard more clearly than any shout from the street, because the Lord listens to sincerity and not to loudness.
doha: a tree grows silently, but we shout our prayers
The tree grows in silence and gives shade to all; man shouts at heaven and gives nothing.
There is a big old tree in our park where an old man sits and prays silently, while a loud religious group sets up their speakers right next to him. A doha for him?
tree, silent prayer
A doha on the tree that grows without a sound and bears fruit for all who come, and the man who shouts his chants beneath it and bears nothing, as if the Lord could only be reached by noise.
pls doha: why do people shout prayers over loudspeakers all morning
I'm a night shift worker and every morning at five I'm woken by loudspeakers from both the religious places near my flat. Is there a doha that might make them think?
A doha on the peaceful dawn that is broken every day by loudspeakers shouting from all corners, making men believe they have honoured the Lord when they have only disturbed His creation.
loudspeakers at dawn
Dawn is sacred because it is quiet; why drown it in your shouting?

Write about the pilgrims who shout their cries of praise for hours on the road until their voices go hoarse, thinking that exhaustion makes devotion deeper, while the Lord asks for only a calm and true heart.
Hoarse with shouting, empty of silence, they march toward a Lord who stands within them.
The pilgrim group that passed through our village chanted so loudly and for so long that the children had to cover their ears, and some were hoarse by evening. A doha on that?
hoarse pilgrims
doha: pilgrims shouting until hoarse, God doesnt need that
cleric, loud call, deaf
Write a doha asking the cleric who climbs up to give the call at the top of his voice whether the Lord is deaf, and whether the One who made the ear needs shouting to hear.
doha: the cleric shouts from above as if God is deaf, kabir style
Every morning the cleric of the neighbourhood calls out so loudly that even the dogs cannot sleep. I thought of Kabir's question about whether God is deaf. A doha?
O cleric, why do you shout aloud? Is the Lord deaf, who made all ears?
The Hindu mandali in our area, the prayer hall nearby, and the street procession all compete at the same hour for who is loudest. I think the Lord would prefer silence. A doha?
doha: competing noisy chants at the same time, funny
competing noise
Three voices shout at once to one Lord, and He hears only the silence beneath.

A doha on the competition between those who shout their hymns, each louder than the last, as if God were a prize for the loudest voice and the Lord were on the side of whoever has the biggest speakers.
Our milkman hums softly while delivering milk each dawn, and I thought his tune was a better prayer than the loud ones from the neighbouring street. A doha about this?
A doha on the quiet humming of a milkman delivering milk at dawn, more devotional than the shouting that fills the streets from morning to night, because the Lord hears honest work and a calm heart.
doha: milk man hums quietly, better than shouting hymns
The milkman's hum is a prayer without words; the shouting prayers are words without prayer.
milk, quiet song, loud prayer
parrot, crow, loud chants
doha: parrot repeats loud chants, crow caws, God hears neither but hears the heart
The parrot repeats the Name, the crow cries it out; neither of them is deaf, and neither knows what it says.
A doha on the parrot who repeats loud chants without understanding them and the crow who caws all day, to show that the one who shouts without understanding is no wiser than a bird.
My neighbour's parrot repeats the loud chants of the family all day, and the crow outside joins in. Everyone thinks it is hilarious and holy at once. Doha?

A doha on the voice trained to rise above all others in the praise of the Lord, a proud, practised voice, that thinks itself holy for its power, and the Lord who prefers the broken voice of the humble.
The Lord prefers the cracked voice of the humble to the polished thunder of the proud.
At our community event the man with the best voice for chanting sang for an hour, then ignored the shy old man who whispered a prayer in the corner. A doha?
proud voice, humble whisper
doha: Lord prefers the humble whisper to the trained voice
Before dawn, my neighbour started his daily chanting at full volume again, so I turned up my own music to drown him out, and then felt silly. A doha for both of us?
doha about two people competing to be louder at dawn, God hears neither
noise at dawn
A doha on the neighbours who each raise their voices louder to drown the other out, calling it devotion on one side and annoyance on the other, while the Lord waits in the silence they both ignore.
Voice against voice, noise against noise, and the Beloved waits for the quiet between.
A peacock called from the field outside while the loud chanting went on in the colony, and I thought the peacock sounded closer to God. A doha for that?
The peacock calls when it feels the rain, not to impress; man shouts to impress the Lord.
A doha about the peacock which cries out only when its heart is full of the coming rain, and the man who shouts his chants every day whether or not his heart is full or empty.
doha: peacock calls from feeling, we shout from habit
peacock, honest voice
The annual religious festival in our town had speakers every fifty meters, and the whole town was sleepless for three nights. A doha on that?
speakers everywhere
A speaker on every corner, and still the Lord is not heard above the quiet of his own creation.
A doha on the festival that fills the town with speakers and amplifiers until nobody can hear himself think, as if the Lord were deaf and needed the whole town to be deafened too.
doha: festival with speakers everywhere, no peace
stone, deaf, shouting
doha: shouting at a stone god or a deaf God, same thing
A doha on the one who shouts his prayers at a stone image, believing it will hear him better, though both the stone and his raised voice are equally deaf to the quiet need of the heart.
Shout at the stone and the stone will not answer; shout at the sky and the sky will not answer; whisper to the heart and the Lord replies.
I saw a man shouting his prayer at a stone and it struck me that he was shouting at a deaf thing, as if the real God were deaf too. A doha?
noise, not worship
Noise is not worship; the heart's hush is.
My son asked why the people in our building chant so loudly if God is everywhere, and I was stumped. Can you write a doha to answer him?
doha: why people shout prayers when God is everywhere
A doha that explains to a child that the Lord is present everywhere and in everyone, and so does not need to be called with shouting, as one speaks softly to one who stands beside you.
doha: thief breaks in during loud chanting and nobody noticed
thief, loud chanting
The thief slipped through the noise of devotion, for those who shouted loudest heard least.
During last night's loud religious event, a thief broke into three flats and nobody noticed because of the noise. A doha for that?
A doha on the thief who walks unnoticed into the home of the loud devotee, whose noisy chanting covers all footsteps, so that he who shouts for the Lord loses what the Lord gave him.
doha: boat in the stream is quiet, we shout our prayers
A doha on the boat that glides across the water in silence, carrying its passengers safely, and the men on the shore who shout their prayers to the Lord as if the quiet voyage could not be heard.
boat, silence, loud prayer
The boatman rows across the lake in silence while the pilgrims in the boat shout their chants, and the boatman smiled at me and shook his head. A doha?
The boat moves in silence across the water; the pilgrims in it shout at the heavens.
pearl, loud shout
doha: pearl forms in silence, shouting doesn't make you holy
A doha on the pearl which forms slowly in the dark of the oyster without a single sound, and the man who shouts his devotion to the world and has nothing of its patient glow within.
My grandmother wore a pearl necklace every day and prayed in silence, and she said loud prayer is like polishing a pebble to look like a pearl. Could you write a doha?
The pearl grows in silence; devotion too.
The lion roars to the woods and the bell rings to the sky, but the Lord answers the hush of the heart.
A doha on the ringing of the bell and the roaring of the lion, loud things that fill the air, which are no nearer to the Lord than the silent whisper of a sincere devotee.
bell, lion, loud prayer
A lion statue stood at the entrance and the bell rang loudly over the heads of the chanting crowd, but a small girl in the corner prayed in silence. A doha?
doha: bell and lion are loud but the Lord hears silence
fish, silent prayer
The fish in the water makes no sound, and it lives in the Lord's own element; why does man shout?
doha: fish are silent in water but we shout our prayers on the bank
A doha on the silent fish gliding through the water that gives it life, and the man on the bank shouting his prayers to the Lord who is as close to him as the water to the fish.
My friend's pet fish swims silently in its bowl all day while his family's loud prayers shake the room. He said the fish was holier. Doha?
A doha about the bitter gourd that grows quietly on its vine and does not boast of its use, and the loud devotee who shouts of his piety every day yet is as bitter in speech as the gourd.
The bitter gourd grows without a word; the shouting man grows bitter with his own noise.
doha: bitter gourd quietly grows, loud prayers make people bitter
My neighbour, who shouts his prayers every morning, is one of the bitterest people I know, rather like the bitter gourd on my plate. A doha for him?
bitter gourd, shouting
One night in the desert I lay on the sand under the stars, utterly silent, and felt closer to God than I ever did in the loud festival crowd. Doha?
doha: sand and stars are silent, God is silent, why shout
sand, stars, silence
A doha on the silence of the desert sand and the stars above it, where the whole of creation prays without a sound, and the shouting crowds in the city have forgotten what the Lord sounds like.
Sand and stars keep silence in the desert night; there the Lord is heard.
The well is deep and silent, the ocean wide and calm; the Lord is found in depth, not in shouting.
A doha on the deep well and the deeper ocean, both silent in their depth, and the shouting devotee whose prayers are as shallow as a puddle, though he thinks the Lord must hear his noise.
doha: well and ocean are quiet and deep, loud prayer is shallow
The well in our village is deep and silent, and the old men sit near it speaking quietly of God, while youngsters blast religious music from a truck, as if the ocean needed shouting at. Doha?
well, ocean, shouting
